bullets: Culture is a system that never sits still — a heuristic grounded in patterns observed at teams using Substack and reportedly holding across three different teams.
Drift can only be noticed rather than gripped; attempts to control it directly miss how it actually operates.
Second-order effects are the most overlooked dimension of cultural drift — the part most people miss when reasoning about how culture changes.
Ignoring cultural drift carries a concrete cost: teams end up rebuilding it from scratch a year later rather than adapting incrementally.
Systems thinking cross-cuts every aspect of cultural drift — its trade-offs shape the rest of the analysis rather than forming a separate topic.
Practical adoption favors small experiments over sweeping change — pick one idea, run it for two weeks, and treat the rest as iteration.
